According to new data from Tussell, UK public bodies paid private consultants £3.4 billion in 2023-24, representing a 62% increase (£1.3 billion) compared to 2019-20 levels. This spending surge that began during the pandemic has not returned to pre-Covid amounts, creating a significant challenge for Keir Starmer's government, which has pledged to reduce consultant spending by half during this parliamentary term.

Since Labour took office, nearly £650 million in new consultant contracts have been awarded, including a major deal with KPMG worth up to £223 million for civil service training over 15 months. Many of these contracts were agreed upon before the government transition.

Labour peer Prem Sikka criticized this trend as part of a problematic culture of relying on consultants, arguing that external advisors cannot effectively understand complex organizations and provide meaningful solutions in short timeframes.
